title: Compañía Minera Coimolache entrega moderno centro de salud en el distrito de Chugur en Cajamarca
summary: El nuevo centro de salud cuenta con una moderna infraestructura y equipos de última generación. Además, se ha equipado y capacitado al personal para brindar el servicio de Telemedicina a […]
body_text: El nuevo centro de salud cuenta con una moderna infraestructura y equipos de última generación. Además, se ha equipado y capacitado al personal para brindar el servicio de Telemedicina a modo de piloto. Se espera que el nuevo centro de salud brinde servicio de salud de calidad a los más de 3 mil habitantes del distrito de Chugur y a las comunidades cercanas. Compañía Minera Coimolache, parte de Compañía de Minas Buenaventura, inauguró hoy un nuevo centro de salud en el distrito de Chugur, provincia de Hualgayoc, Cajamarca, en un evento que reunió a directivos de Compañía de Minas Buenaventura, autoridades del Gobierno Regional y de la Municipalidad Distrital de Chugur. Esta obra se hizo realidad como parte del “Proyecto Ampliación y Mejoramiento de los Servicios del Centro de Salud de Chugur”, que busca mejorar la atención en salud de la población chugurana. El nuevo centro de salud beneficiará aproximadamente a más de 3 mil habitantes del mencionado distrito y comunidades cercanas. La construcción de este nuevo centro de salud se llevó a cabo como parte del Convenio de Cooperación entre el Gobierno Regional de Cajamarca, responsable de las políticas en favor de la salud en la región, Compañía Minera Coimolache, que se encargó del financiamiento integral y ejecución del proyecto, y la Asociación Los Andes de Cajamarca, que se encargó de administrar el fondo. El desarrollo del proyecto tuvo los siguientes componentes: 1.- Compra y saneamiento del terreno, 2.- Estudios de perfil y desarrollo de expediente técnico, 3.- Ejecución de la obra de infraestructura, 4.- Capacitación del personal, y 5.- Implementación de mobiliario, equipamiento médico e informático. A la fecha se ha ejecutado al 100% todos los componentes y hoy 9 de abril se realizó la transferencia y donación al Gobierno Regional para que el centro de salud esté al servicio de la población. Cabe destacar que todos los componentes del proyecto fueron diseñados y ejecutados siguiendo la normativa actual del sector salud. Adicionalmente, Compañía Minera Coimolache realizó la entrega de equipos, software y capacitación al personal, con la finalidad de implementar el servicio de Telemedicina a modo de piloto para todo el primer nivel de atención en la región. El moderno centro de salud ha sido equipado para brindar los siguientes servicios: medicina general, medicina familiar, control prenatal, atención al recién nacido, puerperio y planificación familiar, radiología, odontología general, sala de partos, consultorio TBC, tópico de urgencias y emergencias, laboratorios de hematología/bioquímica y de microbiología, entre otros servicios. “Desde Buenaventura y Coimolache nos sentimos orgullosos de entregar esta obra que busca mejorar de manera importante la atención primaria de la salud en Chugur. Estamos nuevamente frente a un claro ejemplo de que el trabajo conjunto entre la empresa y las autoridades permite que las obras realmente importantes para la población se hagan realidad. No somos casilleros estancos, tenemos que trabajar juntos. El Perú necesita de todos. Hoy celebramos el resultado de ese trabajo que contó con el compromiso de las autoridades para ponerlo en funcionamiento. Espero que los peruanos podamos integrarnos más para trabajar todos juntos”, señaló Roque Benavides, presidente del Directorio de Buenaventura, quien estuvo presente en el acto de inauguración.

title: Crowe LLP Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply
summary: Everything you need to land a Crowe LLP internship in 2027–2028, programs in audit, tax, and consulting, eligibility, deadlines, the interview process, and tips to stand out.
body_text: Crowe LLP Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply Last updated: July 2026 Crowe LLP is the 12th-largest US accounting firm by revenue , with $1.28 billion in net revenue and more than 5,000 specialists across 40 US offices . It just locked in a $3 billion equity investment from KKR , making it one of the largest accounting firms to take private-equity backing. And unlike the Big 4, Crowe publishes no GPA minimum on any internship posting. For the 2027–2028 cycle, Winter 2027 Audit and Tax Intern postings are already live on Crowe's Workday portal, with the Tax Intern deadline set for September 30, 2026. Both postings warn they may close before that date, so the runway is shorter than it looks. Quick Facts Fact Detail Where to apply careers.crowe.com/student-careers . Join the Talent Network for opening alerts Application window (2027–28) Winter 2027 postings live now; Tax deadline September 30, 2026. Summer 2027 postings expected spring 2027 Rolling? Effectively yes. JDs state applications accepted "on an ongoing basis" but may close before the stated deadline Eligibility Pursuing Bachelor's or Master's in Accounting or similar; CPA eligibility required (150 credit hours); no visa sponsorship Duration 8–10 weeks (summer); January–March (winter audit busy season) Compensation $27–$42/hr official posted range; Glassdoor average ~$35/hr Return offers No published rate; official: internships are the "number one pipeline for full-time hires" plus a starting bonus Locations Chicago (HQ), plus 39 other US offices including Los Angeles, Denver, Atlanta, New York, Dallas, and Fort Lauderdale # Programs Audit & Assurance, Tax, Consulting, Advisory, Enabling Functions, and Crowe Studio The two things that separate Crowe from the Big 4: no published GPA cutoff anywhere, and an effectively rolling application that can close without warning. CPA eligibility (150 credit hours) is the hard requirement, not your transcript. Externships are short, remote professional experience programs where you finish a real project with a real company. The Attronica FP&A & Private Company Valuation Externship and the Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship build exactly the Excel modeling and data analytics evidence Crowe's audit and tax JDs ask for. Explore all Externships . What Is a Crowe LLP Internship? A Crowe LLP internship is a paid, 8-to-10-week placement that puts accounting students into real audit, tax, consulting, or advisory engagements at one of the firm's 40 US offices . Crowe has been named to Glassdoor's 100 Best Places to Work multiple years running and appeared on the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For list six times . Interns rate the firm 3.7 out of 5 on Glassdoor . As part of the Crowe Global network , the firm connects to over 200 independent firms across 130 countries, and its official internship page calls the program the "number one pipeline for full-time hires," with a starting bonus for those who convert. When Do Crowe LLP Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028? Crowe's recruiting calendar runs in two tracks: winter internships (January through March, recruited in summer and fall) and summer internships (June through August, recruited in spring). The Winter 2027 Audit and Tax Intern postings are already live as of mid-2026, with the Tax posting carrying a September 30, 2026 deadline . But both postings warn they accept applications "on an ongoing basis" and "may close before the stated closing date," so the real deadline is whenever the seats fill. Summer 2027 intern postings are expected to appear around spring 2027, recruited through campus career fairs. Now · Summer 2026 you're HERE Winter 2027 Audit and Tax Intern postings are live on Crowe's Workday portal right now. Both accept applications on an ongoing basis but may close early. This is the apply-and-build window: what's on your resume when a recruiter opens your file decides whether you get the 30-minute interview. The Attronica FP&A & Private Company Valuation Externship and the Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship are remote, real-company projects that give a September application finished work to point at. September 30, 2026 ROLLING — APPLY WEEK 1 Published deadline for Tax Intern Winter 2027. The Audit posting has no stated end date, but both warn of early closure. Campus career fairs begin in August, and Crowe recruits heavily through on-campus events. January–March 2027 Winter internships run during busy season. Audit interns work across client financials, transactions, and internal controls; tax interns prepare returns and conduct research. Expect approximately 40 hours per week, with some overtime during peak periods. Spring 2027 EXPECTED Summer 2027 intern postings are expected here, recruited through spring campus events. Crowe typically posts roles on its Workday portal and recruits at campus career fairs. Summer 2028 postings would follow in fall 2027. Summer 2027 Summer internships run 8–10 weeks, June to August. Perform well: Crowe calls internships its "number one pipeline for full-time hires," and interns offered a full-time position also receive a starting bonus. Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open Both live Crowe Workday JDs include the same two lines: "Crowe accepts applications for this role on an ongoing basis" and "This job may close before the stated closing date, you're encouraged to apply as soon as possible." That isn't boilerplate. The Tax Winter 2027 posting carries a September 30 deadline, but it may fill before that. The Audit Winter 2027 posting has no stated end date at all. When a posting is rolling and can close without warning, the application date itself becomes a filter. Crowe's campus recruiting page confirms that most interviews are virtual and about 30 minutes long, and one Reddit user reported getting an offer "a few hours after my interview." The process moves fast once your file is picked up, which means the earliest applicants face the most open seats and the shortest wait. Which Crowe LLP Internship Programs Should You Target? Crowe offers internships across its core service lines, with Audit & Assurance and Tax being the largest and most actively recruited tracks. The student careers page also lists Consulting, Advisory, Enabling Functions, and Crowe Studio. Program Focus Duration Key skills Audit & Assurance Audit client financials, transactions, and internal controls across manufacturing, healthcare, government, financial institutions, and not-for-profit sectors 8–10 weeks (winter: Jan–Mar; summer: Jun–Aug) Excel, data analytics, analytical skills, communication, CPA track Tax Tax return preparation, basic tax research, domestic and international engagements across manufacturing, retail, construction, real estate, and financial institutions 8–10 weeks (winter & summer) Excel, tax concepts, research, problem-solving, CPA track Consulting Consulting engagements across firm clients Varies (typically summer) Problem-solving, communication, teamwork Advisory Advisory services across the firm's client base Varies Analytical skills, communication See all pathways on the student careers page . And note the seasonal split: winter (busy season) internships run January through March and are recruited in summer and fall, while summer internships are recruited through spring campus events. Both Audit and Tax run in both seasons. What Are the Eligibility Requirements? Crowe publishes the same core requirements on every intern posting: • Degree: pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's in Accounting, Tax, or a similar degree. Both the Audit and Tax JDs specify this. • CPA eligibility (required): you must be on track to meet the educational requirements to sit for the CPA exam in your assigned Crowe work location. This typically means 150 credit hours, and requirements vary by state. This must be fulfilled before starting a full-time role. • GPA: no minimum is published on any Crowe internship posting. The JDs say "strong academic credentials" without specifying a number. • Work authorization: every posting carries the same line: "Crowe isn't sponsoring for work authorization at this time." No visa sponsorship is available. • Skills: Excel proficiency is required across all tracks. Data analytics experience is "strongly desired" for audit. Both tracks require strong verbal and written communication, willingness to travel, and flexibility for evenings or weekends when needed. Does Crowe Have a GPA Cutoff? No, and that's verified absence rather than omission: neither the Audit Winter 2027 JD nor the Tax Winter 2027 JD publishes a number. This is unusual among top-15 accounting firms, many of which set a 3.0 or 3.2 floor. The real gatekeeper is CPA eligibility: you need the 150 credit hours your state requires before starting full-time. The other hard stop is the no-sponsorship line, which excludes international students who need work authorization. Beyond those two, Crowe weighs Excel proficiency, relevant experience, leadership, and the behavioral interview. What Skills Does Crowe LLP Look For, and How Do You Build Them? Only two 2027 intern JDs are live in full text (Audit Winter and Tax Winter), but they are strikingly consistent about what Crowe screens for. Excel proficiency shows up in both. So do communication, leadership, problem-solving, and time management. The split comes at the technical layer: audit wants data analytics experience ("strongly desired") and comfort with "advanced analytics, data visualizations and process flow automation," while tax wants foundational tax concepts and research skills. What does that tell you? Crowe hires CPA-track generalists who can talk to clients and work in Excel, then trains the vertical. The missing line is just as telling: no coding, no specific software certifications, no standardized test scores. Small sample (n=2); counts reflect shared requirements across both roles. Prior-cycle basis; skill weights may shift as summer and consulting postings appear. How Is Demand for Accounting Interns Moving Right Now? Accounting intern hiring context: July 2026 Market context for accounting-intern candidates · compensation data from Crowe JDs and aggregators ▲ Crowe pays above market: the $27–$42/hr official range puts Crowe interns roughly 29% above the national average for tax interns ( Indeed ) ★ CPA-track interns carry a premium: firms requiring 150-credit-hour eligibility consistently post higher ranges than general accounting-intern roles, and Crowe's Glassdoor average of ~$35/hr confirms the premium = The bench you convert into is deep: Crowe calls internships its "number one pipeline for full-time hires," and interns who convert also receive a starting bonus Crowe's above-average pay and explicit full-time pipeline make it a strong mid-tier target, especially for candidates who want busy-season audit or tax exposure without the Big 4 grind. Method: compensation data from Crowe's Winter 2027 Workday JDs, cross-referenced with Glassdoor ($35/hr avg) and Indeed ($34/hr tax intern avg) aggregates, July 2026. Market context is directional, not exhaustive. Build These Skills Before You Apply And every skill in the chart maps to a remote Externship where you finish a real company project before the window closes. Skill (from real JDs) JD evidence Externship that builds it Excel & financial modeling Both JDs: "proficient with Excel"; Audit JD: "audit client financials, transactions and internal control processes" Attronica FP&A & Private Company Valuation Data analytics & visualization Audit JD: "data analytics experience strongly desired," "advanced analytics, data visualizations and process flow automation" Beats by Dre Data Analytics Analytical & problem-solving skills Both JDs: "sharpen your analytical skills," "problem-solving"; Tax JD: "basic tax research" Yinan Zhao Investing & Financial Modeling How close is the overlap? The Attronica deliverable is FP&A work in the vocabulary Crowe's own Audit JD uses, and the data analytics both the Attronica and Beats by Dre Externships end on covers the one skill Crowe calls "strongly desired." Every Externship ends with a presented deliverable, which is the "strong verbal and written communication" line item both JDs share. What Is the Crowe LLP Application and Interview Process Like? Crowe's interview funnel is shorter and more behavioral than most large firms, with no standardized technical test: 1. Apply at careers.crowe.com/student-careers with a resume, either through the online portal or at a campus career fair. Crowe recruits actively at campus events in fall and spring. 2. Virtual video interview, approximately 30 minutes. Crowe's campus recruiting page says most interviews are done virtually via video and focus on work history, educational background, and extracurricular involvement. Some candidates report a pre-recorded video screen with four behavioral questions as an initial filter (community-reported). 3. Possible second interview or office visit. The campus recruiting page notes: "it's our hope that you will be able to visit your preferred Crowe office." The recruiting team contacts candidates with next steps after the initial interview. 4. Offer decision. Reportedly fast. One Reddit user said they got the offer a few hours after the interview . If you have an expiring offer from another firm, Crowe says to let your recruiter know to request an expedited process. There is no formal online assessment, HireVue AI scoring, or technical test for accounting intern roles. Glassdoor confirms the process is "generally straightforward, typically involving initial screenings followed by one to two interviews focusing on behavioral questions." Rehearse the behavioral rounds: our HireVue question guide with a free AI mock tool runs the same time pressure even though Crowe's format is live, not recorded. What Students on Reddit Say Three threads show the process and the job from the inside. All you need to do is show up on time, ask questions, take notes, apply what you learned before to the next task, and you'll do a good job. r/Accounting intern advice thread, paraphrased · read the thread I interviewed with Crowe a week ago, and they were really fast at replying back. Literally got the offer a few hours after my interview. r/Accounting candidate report, paraphrased · read the thread Just accepted my Crowe Audit Internship. Was wondering about the typical hours. Reply: I did 55 a week. My internship was extended for the summer. r/Accounting intern experience thread, paraphrased · read the thread How Do You Stand Out at a Firm That Skips the GPA Line? Three moves, all executable before September. First, apply within the first week a posting goes live; Crowe's rolling review means the earliest applicants face the least competition, and both JDs warn the role may close early. Second, get the CPA-eligibility question sorted now: it's the one hard requirement Crowe will not bend on, and state rules vary on credit hours. Third, bring evidence in the JD's exact vocabulary. A finished data analytics project answers "tell me about your analytical skills" with a deliverable instead of an anecdote, and it covers the one skill Crowe calls "strongly desired." The interview is purely behavioral with no technical test, so the proof you bring in your resume is the only technical signal in the room. And remember the program's stated goal is conversion. Interview like someone auditioning for the full-time seat, because you're. What Other Companies Should You Consider? Crowe's peer set clusters around the mid-tier accounting firms: larger than regional shops, smaller than the Big 4, and often offering more direct client exposure during internships. BDO USA IPA #5; larger mid-tier with similar audit and tax tracks and a global network Careers site RSM US IPA #6; middle-market focus with strong advisory and consulting intern programs Careers site Grant Thornton IPA #7; similar size with a reputation for earlier intern responsibility Careers site Baker Tilly IPA #9; also recently took PE investment; similar culture and client mix Careers site All four recruit on similar campus timelines and offer comparable pay ranges. The differentiator is usually office location and industry-sector exposure. If Crowe's 40-office footprint doesn't cover your target city, one of these firms might. FAQ When do Crowe internship applications open for 2027–2028? Crowe's Winter 2027 Audit and Tax Intern postings went live by mid-2026, with the Tax Intern deadline set for September 30, 2026. Crowe typically recruits at campus career fairs in fall for winter and spring starts and in spring for summer starts. Join Crowe's Talent Network at careers.crowe.com for alerts on new openings. Are Crowe internship applications rolling? Effectively yes. Both live postings state Crowe "accepts applications for this role on an ongoing basis" and warn the posting "may close before the stated closing date." Applying as soon as the posting goes live improves your chances, particularly during busy season when audit and tax teams fill positions quickly. What GPA do you need for a Crowe internship? Crowe doesn't list a minimum GPA in its internship job descriptions. The JDs call for "strong academic credentials" without specifying a number. The firm places greater emphasis on CPA eligibility (150 credit hours), Excel proficiency, relevant experience, and demonstrated leadership and communication skills over a GPA cutoff. What is the Crowe internship interview process like? Crowe's campus recruiting page says most interviews are done "virtually via video" and last about 30 minutes. Questions focus on work history, educational background, and extracurricular involvement. Some candidates report a pre-recorded video screen with four behavioral questions first. There are typically no technical tests for accounting intern roles. Do Crowe interns get return offers? Crowe's internship page states that its internships "tend to be a direct pipeline for full-time hires" and that interns offered a full-time position also receive a starting bonus. No specific return-offer rate is published. Reddit users report offers coming quickly, sometimes hours after the final interview, reinforcing that the pipeline is strong. What skills does Crowe look for in interns? Crowe's JDs emphasize Excel proficiency, strong academic credentials, leadership, problem-solving, and verbal and written communication skills. For audit interns, data analytics experience is "strongly desired." Both audit and tax interns must be on track for CPA eligibility. The firm values Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship in its culture. Are Crowe internships paid? Yes. The official wage range is $27 to $42 per hour, varying by skills, experience, and location. Glassdoor reports an average of about $35 per hour for Crowe interns, and Indeed pegs tax interns at roughly $34 per hour. Interns offered a full-time position also receive a starting bonus. Benefits include paid time off and medical incentives. Does Crowe sponsor visas for interns? No. Every Crowe internship posting states "Crowe isn't sponsoring for work authorization at this time." This applies across all service lines and locations. International students who need sponsorship should explore OPT or CPT options with their university's international student office, or look at firms that do sponsor. Crowe reviews applications on an ongoing basis and fills positions before deadlines close. Build proof while the window is open: a remote Externship turns "proficient with Excel" from a self-assessment into a finished project a recruiter can verify. About the Author Bifei Wang has spent 17 years focused on human flow and the growth of young professionals, spanning international education, career training and coaching, and recruitment process outsourcing. Over 7 years at Extern, he has had one-on-one sessions with thousands of students exploring careers in consulting, finance, tech, marketing, and data, giving him a firsthand view of how the job market has shifted for early-career professionals and what it actually takes to break in.

title: How to Streamline the Permitting Process (And Why It’s So Critical)
summary: Learn how to save time on permitting — and why streamlining permitting matters so much for contractors and builders today.
body_text: In the world of construction and development, the permitting process is a necessary but often frustrating hurdle. While it’s essential for ensuring safety and compliance with local regulations, permitting is notorious for causing delays, miscommunications, and inefficiencies that can ripple through the entire project lifecycle. For contractors, developers, and architects alike, navigating the layers of bureaucracy, managing fluctuating timelines, and dealing with endless paperwork can feel overwhelming. The process can stall projects, drain resources, and add significant costs to the bottom line. But there’s a better way. Using permitting software to streamline the permitting process can help you avoid delays, improve collaboration, and ultimately, deliver better project outcomes. With the right approach and the help of technology, you can turn permitting from a roadblock into a manageable part of your workflow. ‍ The Hidden Costs of Delays and Inefficiencies Delays in the permitting process often stem from a combination of factors—slow approval processes, incomplete documentation, miscommunication between stakeholders, and sometimes even a lack of transparency on the part of municipal authorities. Unfortunately, these delays aren’t just minor inconveniences; they can have serious consequences for your project’s timeline and budget. Every day a project is held up waiting for permit approval is a day when resources sit idle, deadlines are missed, and teams are left in limbo. Subcontractors might have to reschedule, materials might go unused, and labor costs start to pile up. In a competitive market, where timing is everything, these kinds of disruptions can diminish the overall value of a project and reduce profitability. Let’s look at some specific areas where these delays can cost your business: 1. Labor and Equipment Costs When projects are delayed, the costs start to add up quickly. Labor crews may be left without work, but wages still need to be paid. Equipment that’s on-site may sit unused, incurring rental fees or depreciating in value. Every extra day of delay can significantly eat into profit margins and strain your budget. 2. Client Trust and Satisfaction Clients expect projects to be completed on time and within budget. Repeated delays due to permitting issues can erode client trust and damage your reputation. In an industry that thrives on referrals and long-term relationships, ensuring that your projects stay on track is critical for future business. 3. Lost Opportunities Every delay is a missed opportunity to move on to the next project. If a permit drags on for weeks or months, it can push back your entire pipeline, creating bottlenecks for future work. This can prevent you from capitalizing on market opportunities or tackling new projects that are ready to go. Ultimately, the more efficient your permitting process, the more likely you are to maintain strong relationships with clients, stay within budget, and keep your projects moving forward. ‍ The Transparency Gap in Traditional Project Management One of the most challenging aspects of traditional project management, particularly when it comes to permitting, is the lack of visibility into where things stand. Too often, contractors, developers, and other key stakeholders find themselves in the dark about the status of their permits. This can happen for a variety of reasons—sometimes municipal authorities are slow to update their records, or maybe the information isn’t properly communicated to the project manager. In other cases, important details get lost in email threads or phone calls, making it difficult to track where things stand. In a world where real-time updates are the norm in many industries, construction permitting has often lagged behind. Without visibility into the permit’s progress, you’re left wondering when (or if) it will be approved, and your team can’t make informed decisions about how to move forward. ‍ Why Transparency Matters Transparency is more than just a buzzword—it’s a crucial element of effective project management. When all parties involved in the construction process have clear, real-time insight into the permitting status, it becomes much easier to manage timelines, expectations, and resources. For example, if a contractor knows exactly when a permit is expected to be approved, they can schedule labor and materials accordingly, avoiding the costly disruptions that come from unexpected delays. If there’s a holdup in the approval process, having visibility into that issue allows the team to address it immediately, rather than discovering the problem too late. ‍ Leveraging Technology to Simplify Approvals This is where modern technology comes into play. Building permit management platforms are designed to centralize and streamline the entire process, making it easier for all stakeholders to track, collaborate, and communicate effectively. ‍ Real-Time Updates and Notifications One of the biggest advantages of using a digital permitting platform is real-time updates. As soon as a permit is submitted, processed, or approved, the relevant stakeholders are notified immediately. This transparency allows teams to be proactive rather than reactive. For example, let’s say a project requires multiple permits for different stages of construction. Instead of waiting for an email or phone call to find out whether a permit has been approved, a contractor can check the platform and see exactly where the permit stands in the process. This visibility reduces uncertainty and helps project managers make more informed decisions. Additionally, real-time notifications allow teams to coordinate without needing to constantly meet or communicate. When everyone has access to the same information, it becomes much easier to keep things on track. ‍ Centralized Documentation Another challenge in traditional permitting processes is managing the sheer volume of paperwork required. From blueprints and environmental assessments to zoning approvals and inspection reports, keeping track of every document can be overwhelming. With a permit management platform, all documentation is centralized in one location. This eliminates the need to sift through email chains or dig through filing cabinets to find the latest version of a document. Instead, everything is stored in the cloud, where it can be easily accessed, shared, and updated by all parties involved. This centralization not only reduces administrative headaches but also helps prevent errors, such as submitting outdated or incorrect documents, which can lead to further delays. ‍ Building a Stronger Reputation with Efficient Permitting In an industry where reputation is everything, efficient permitting can be a key differentiator. Clients and partners expect timely communication, accurate information, and a clear path forward when it comes to project management. If you can consistently deliver on these expectations, you’ll build a reputation as a reliable and trustworthy contractor or developer. ‍ Proactive Communication with Stakeholders One of the best ways to protect your reputation is by maintaining proactive communication with your clients and stakeholders. Rather than waiting for issues to arise, anticipate them and keep everyone informed throughout the permitting process. By using a permit management platform, you can provide regular updates and address potential delays before they become major problems. ‍ Delivering on Deadlines Meeting deadlines is one of the best ways to prove your reliability. With a more efficient permitting process, you’ll be able to keep projects on schedule and avoid the costly delays that can harm your reputation. Whether you’re working on a residential development or a large-scale commercial project, timely permit approvals help you maintain control over your timelines and budget. ‍ Strategic Benefits of Transparent Project Management For contractors and developers, a more transparent and streamlined permitting process offers several strategic advantages: Fewer Delays: When all stakeholders have access to real-time updates and the same set of information, you can minimize the risk of miscommunication and missed deadlines. Increased Client and Vendor Trust: A transparent process helps build trust with clients and external vendors. They’ll know they can rely on your team to deliver accurate timelines and clear communication throughout the project. More Consistent Revenue: With more efficient workflows, you’ll be able to take on more projects, leading to more consistent and reliable revenue streams. Business Growth Opportunities: As your reputation for efficiency grows, so do your business opportunities. With a solid foundation in place, you’ll be better positioned to expand into new markets and tackle larger projects. ‍ Ready to Transform Your Permitting Process? Streamlining the permitting process isn’t just about reducing delays—it’s about creating a more transparent, efficient, and reliable workflow that benefits everyone involved. By leveraging technology and improving communication, you can take control of your project timelines, reduce costs, and build stronger relationships with clients and stakeholders. Download the eBook to discover how you can simplify your permitting process, save time, and avoid costly delays.

How flight compensation works outside the US In much of the world, air passenger rights are taken seriously. The most important regulation for US travelers is EC 261/2004 , also known as EU 261 (and its UK twin, UK 261). These laws require airlines to compensate passengers if their disruption was the airline’s fault, but doesn’t cover disruptions caused by extraordinary circumstances like severe weather. Compensation applies to: Delays over 3 hours Last-minute cancellations Denied boarding due to overbooking For flights covered by EC 261 or UK 261, payouts range from $270 to $650 per passenger . That can quickly add up for families or groups traveling together. Europe isn’t the only region with strong passenger protection. Brazil’s ANAC 400 also promises compensation and care when flights are delayed, cancelled, or rescheduled, and it applies to both domestic and international flights departing from Brazil. Airlines, of course, try their best to avoid paying. They rely on passengers not knowing their rights, or giving up after too much paperwork. title: Nike and Hyperice Debut the Nike Air Zoom Hyperslide: An Innovative Recovery Slide for All Athletes
summary: The Nike Air Zoom Hyperslide combines low-profile Nike Air Zoom cushioning with Hyperice recovery technology, delivering targeted heat and vibration across the top of the foot to help reduce tension, relax feet and support everyday recovery.
body_text: Nike is advancing its commitment to athlete* recovery with the introduction of the Nike Air Zoom Hyperslide, the latest footwear innovation developed in partnership with Hyperice to help athletes easily unwind from the ground up after sport, training, travel and everything in between. The Air Zoom Hyperslide reflects both companies’ belief that performance doesn’t end when competition or training stops. As the demands of sport continue to evolve, athletes are increasingly prioritizing recovery as part of their complete routine, looking for solutions that help them bounce back from the rigors of sport and everyday life. The Air Zoom Hyperslide meets that need head-on, combining Nike’s footwear expertise with Hyperice recovery technology in a wearable, mobile slide built to help athletes move and perform better and ultimately get back to what they love. Built to make recovery easier to work into the flow of competition, training or daily life, the Air Zoom Hyperslide pairs a low-profile, full-length Air Zoom sole for soft, responsive comfort with targeted Hyperice heat and vibration across the top of the foot to help reduce tension, relax feet and support everyday recovery. At the center of the recovery experience is a removable, magnetic Hyperslide Pod housed within the slide’s adjustable strap. The pod delivers three levels of heat (reaching 117 F / 47 C) , and three levels of vibration and runs in 15-minute recovery cycles, giving athletes the ability to seamlessly customize their experience through on-pod controls or by connecting to the Hyperice App. “Athletes leave everything on the field, and the approach to recovery needs to meet them at the same level,” says Tobie Hatfield, Senior Director of Athlete Innovation, Nike. “With the Nike Air Zoom Hyperslide, we wanted to create a solution that kickstarts recovery the moment you power it up — helping athletes feel more relaxed, restored and ready to take their performance to the next level.” Every aspect of the innovation and design is informed by feedback from both elite and everyday athletes, who called out the unique combination of cushioning, heat and vibration technology — and how quickly the slide impacts their recovery. “It’s the combination that stands out,” says Virgil van Dijk, Nike and Hyperice athlete. “The Hyperice heat and vibration help my feet recover as quickly as possible, while the Nike Air Zoom cushioning makes it feel incredibly comfortable.” The Air Zoom Hyperslide is the second innovation born from the ongoing partnership between Nike and Hyperice, which brings together two brands with a shared commitment to helping athletes move and perform better throughout training and competition. “Our partnership with Nike has always been driven by a shared commitment to innovation for the athlete,” says Anthony Katz, Founder, Hyperice. “With the Nike Air Zoom Hyperslide, we’re making premium recovery more accessible than ever, combining Nike’s iconic footwear expertise with Hyperice technology to help people recover smarter with every step.” Both the Air Zoom Hyperslide and the Nike x Hyperice Hyperboot reflect Nike’s longstanding dedication to serving the complete athlete, from their training and performance during competition to the moments in between, helping make athletes better by pushing what’s possible through innovation and design. The Nike Air Zoom Hyperslide will be available beginning September 29 in select markets at nike.com , hyperice.com and select retail locations globally. *If you have a body, you are an athlete.
